title: Transactional Interval Architecture Technical Reference

primary_frozen_owners.role: transaction trial, rejection, retry, rollback and accepted-state commit authority
requested canonical interval orchestration and external publication authority

qualification_chain.status_a_preservation: docs/status-a/TRACEABILITY.md transaction architecture row plus same-tree F-GC29 and permanent transactional/oracle/mass/numerical suites

permitted_claims: attempts originate from a clone/checkpoint of committed transaction state and captured attempt context
solver failure, incomplete or excessive mass residual, and temporal rejection restore checkpoint context and follow bounded retry policy
the external full-versus-two-half route accepts and commits the two-half candidate only after solver, mass and temporal gates pass
the qualified model-certificate route follows the same candidate-to-accepted discipline with its own temporal certificate gate
accepted transaction state is distinct from externally published canonical interval state
canonical runtime advances accepted internal transactions in a private working state and publishes externally only after the full requested interval completes
failed transaction, no-progress or substep-limit outcomes do not replace the externally committed canonical state
interval mass residual is storage_change minus total_in-minus-total_out and completeness is explicit
retry and rejection diagnostics are accumulated without converting rejected candidate states into committed state
forbidden_claims: no new retry scale, retry budget, temporal tolerance or mass tolerance is defined by F-DOC30
no universal numerical convergence theorem or ACID-database claim
no claim that every future solver or process automatically satisfies these frozen Status-A semantics
no post-Status-A RossFast or later application composition is added to the frozen Status-A denominator
no new concurrent or parallel MultiSWAP semantics
no groundwater-specific staged mass-ledger semantics are generalized into the generic transaction core
no production, reference, test or scientific semantics mutation
